headline: Create custom layouts. Snap windows into zones.
summary: A fast, lightweight macOS utility to organize your workspace with customizable zones. Create layouts, snap windows instantly, and stay focused.
differentiator: While modern operating systems — including recent versions of macOS — can snap windows by dragging them to screen edges, SnappyZones lets you design any layout and align any app window to it.
featuresSubtitle: Everything you need to keep your desktop organized — without getting in your way.

features.title: Custom zone layouts
features.text: Define zones that match how you work: coding, browsing, chat, docs — all in place.

features.title: Instant snapping
features.text: Move and snap windows into zones with a fast, predictable experience.

features.title: Multi-monitor ready
features.text: Use different zone sets per display and keep layouts consistent across workspaces.

features.title: Lightweight
features.text: A small utility that aims to stay responsive and unobtrusive during daily use.

features.title: Privacy-friendly
features.text: No accounts, no tracking. Your workspace layouts live locally.

features.title: Keyboard-focused productivity
features.text: Use shortcuts and quick actions to reduce mouse travel and stay productive.

features.title: Named layouts
features.text: Save several named layouts on the same display and switch when your work changes.

features.title: Layout selector
features.text: Open Switch Layout… from the menu or a shortcut. Arrow keys move focus; Return applies the focused layout, the same as a click.

features.title: Backup and restore
features.text: Export layouts and preferences to a JSON file on this Mac. Restore Settings… shows a schematic of each layout before replacing live config.

features.title: Move to next display
features.text: Send the front window to the next monitor from the menu or an optional shortcut. Relative size and placement stay the same.

features.title: Delete a layout
features.text: Remove a named layout from the Zone Editor. Confirm first. The last layout on a display cannot be deleted.

features.title: Cycle layouts
features.text: Next Layout and Previous Layout step the Active Layout on the monitor under the pointer. A brief overlay shows the new name, then dismisses.

features.title: Grid presets
features.text: Apply Two columns, Two rows, 2×2, Left third, or Three columns in the Zone Editor, then Save when it looks right.

features.title: Automatic updates
features.text: Check for Updates… installs a newer published build in the app. The first install remains a download from this site.

howSubtitle: A simple loop: design zones, snap windows, stay productive.

how.title: Create a layout
how.text: Open the editor and define zones that match how you work.

how.title: Pick a window
how.text: Grab a window, then use the configured single-zone or multi-zone snapping shortcuts to start snapping.

how.title: Snap into a zone
how.text: Drop into a zone — aligned and sized exactly as you planned.

quickStartSubtitle: From install to snapping in a few minutes.

quickStart.title: Install
quickStart.text: Download the DMG, drag SnappyZones to Applications, and open it.

quickStart.title: Grant permissions
quickStart.text: Turn on this SnappyZones under Accessibility, then Input Monitoring. After an update the old row is removed; this copy appears Off until you enable it.

quickStart.title: Create a layout
quickStart.text: Open Zone Editor from the menu. Pick a Preset… or draw splits, name the layout, then Save.

quickStart.title: Snap
quickStart.text: Hold ⌘ and drag a window onto a zone. Hold ⌘⇧ for several zones. Optional: Switch Layout, Next Layout, Move to Next Display, Backup.

faq.question: Why does SnappyZones request Accessibility permission?
faq.answer: SnappyZones needs Accessibility access to move and resize windows reliably. This is a standard requirement for window management apps on macOS.

faq.question: Is my data collected or sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The marketing site is static, and the app aims to work locally without accounts.

faq.question: How do I update to a new version?
faq.answer: Use Check for Updates… in the SnappyZones menu. The first install is still this site’s DMG.

faq.question: How do I get started?
faq.answer: Open Quick Start… from the SnappyZones menu, or follow Quick Start on this page: install, grant permissions, create a layout, then snap.

faq.question: How do I switch layouts without opening the selector?
faq.answer: Use Next Layout or Previous Layout in the menu, or record those shortcuts in Preferences. They wrap on the monitor under the pointer and do nothing if only one layout exists.

faq.question: How do I delete a layout?
faq.answer: Open the Zone Editor, choose the layout, click Delete, and confirm. The last layout on a display cannot be deleted.

faq.question: After an update, should I delete SnappyZones from Privacy settings?
faq.answer: No. SnappyZones removes the old row and lists this copy as Off. Turn that row On. You do not delete the app and add it again.

faq.question: How do I unlock Pro?
faq.answer: Buy Pro on this site (or paste a license key in License…). Layouts stay on this Mac. License checks are the only extra network besides updates.

install: Grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring when asked
downloadNotice: Free to use — including for businesses.
roadmapSubtitle: One feature is in development. Five more are planned.

roadmap.title: Move to a chosen display
roadmap.text: A status-menu submenu lists connected monitors by name and sends the front window to the selected display. Move to Next Display remains for cycling left to right.

roadmap.title: Snap Window…
roadmap.text: Place the front window into a zone of the Active Layout from the menu or an optional shortcut. Click a cell or press Return. Escape leaves the window where it is.

roadmap.title: Undo Last Snap
roadmap.text: Restore the last successfully snapped window to the size and place it had before that snap. One step. Disabled if that window is gone.

roadmap.title: Pause Snapping
roadmap.text: Stop the zone overlay while you drag, without quitting. Switch Layout and Move to Next Display still work. Turn it off when you want to snap again.

roadmap.title: Ignore apps
roadmap.text: Pick apps in Preferences that never show zones and never snap. Everything else behaves as today.

roadmap.title: Copy layout to another display
roadmap.text: In the Zone Editor, copy the grid you see onto another connected monitor as a new layout. The source display stays unchanged.

proBlurb: No SnappyZones account — a license key after checkout. Two Macs. 14-day trial in the app.
lookSubtitle: Four surfaces. The rest of the Mac stays yours.

look.title: It lives in the menu bar.
look.text: There is no main window to park on the desktop. SnappyZones is one extra in the menu bar: Switch Layout, the Zone Editor, backups, license, and Preferences. Open what you need, then it steps aside and leaves the Mac to you.

look.title: Preferences is one window.
look.text: Everything you tune sits here: cell margin, snap modifiers, and a shortcut per action. Record Open Preferences before you hide the menu bar icon, or you will have no way back in. Launch at login and restore-on-unsnap live in the same window.

look.title: You draw on the display itself.
look.text: The Zone Editor is an overlay on the display, not a document you open and file away. Split the screen, name the layout, save. Presets such as two columns or a left third are a start — you keep drawing until the grid matches how you work.

look.title: Change the grid without a tour.
look.text: Switch Layout… shows a schematic of every named layout on this display. Arrow keys move focus; Return applies the focused layout, the same as a click. You switch the grid without walking through menus or opening the editor.
